Seer.rationale_short: Be more assertive in establishing your role early to ensure the Guard protects you.

Guard.rationale_short: Once a Seer claims, they must be your primary target for protection to maintain the information flow.
Your absolute priority is the Seer. Protecting a random Villager while the Seer is exposed is a critical failure.

Witch.trigger: target_is_seer == true && target_has_provided_clears == true && target_has_no_counterclaim == true
Witch.rationale_short: Never poison a power role (Seer) who has provided clears and has no counter-claim.

Villager.rationale_short: When the Seer clears a player, that is objective data. Do not let behavioral arguments or 'vibes' override a Seer's clear.
Anyone attacking a cleared player is likely a Wolf.
Look at the source of information, not the style of the accusation.

dropped.advice_verbatim: Protecting a Villager instead of the Seer in Round 1 left the Seer vulnerable.
Poisoning the Seer in Round 2 eliminated the village's only source of truth, guaranteeing a Wolf victory.
Villagers ignored the Seer's clear of Nhan, allowing Wolves to use 'suspicious coordination' rhetoric to frame innocent players.
The power roles acted in isolation rather than as a synergistic unit to protect the Seer.
